tickets.title: A pi worker runs headless and keeps its session
tickets.what: Spec §2.1.2 "A headless worker…" (22.22). Survey 2026-11-22: 95 of 185 worker jobs (51%) ran brief-to-report with no question, send or repair, but each held a herdr tab; the owner saw 9 tabs. Add a run mode `headless` for continuable roles on the pi harness (imp, general). Selected by `hud_create({ mode: "headless" })` for now; 03 makes it automatic. A headless job opens no tab. It runs pi in its non-interactive JSON mode with a session file in the job dir (not `--no-session`), output appended to a job-dir log, and the same worker MCP tools as a tab worker (hud_report, hud_progress, hud_ask, hud_lease, hud_sonic). It settles on its report like a tab worker and is closed at once (close-on-delivery). `hud_ask` ends the turn and marks the job asking. `hud_respond` then resumes the session (`pi --session <file>`) with the answer as the next message. `hud_send` resumes it the same way, within `resume_s` and otherwise as a repair job, and so do land repairs. Stop (`hud_close`, panel stop) kills the process tree. Reuse headless sonic's spawn/supervision and close-on-delivery's resume helper; do not fork either.

acceptance.text: A synthetic headless imp job runs to a report with no herdr tab and settles closed with its session file kept
hud_ask → hud_respond resumes the same session and the job reports; hud_send after the report resumes within resume_s
A land repair of a headless job resumes its session headless
Stop kills the process tree; progress shows on the card as for tab jobs
Targeted thin-mcp/sonic/close-resume tests pass

Roles with only a CLI place (general on agy, frontend-imp on claude) can then run headless.

tickets.title: The Decision API routes imp work by tier and mode
tickets.what:
Spec §2.1.4 "Imp routing" (22.22). Settings toggle "Imp routing" (off by default), which needs the Decision API like Sonic auto-thinking and reuses its client, budget and fallback code.

Tiers live in the role file, not in code. Add an optional `routing` block to the role-file schema:

```json
"routing": {
  "light":    { "preset": "hydrogen", "use": "mechanical work on an existing pattern: text or doc edits, one or two files, a single test fix, a small bug" },
  "standard": { "use": "an ordinary end-to-end slice" },
  "hard":     { "preset": "astra", "use": "cross-module, concurrency or process lifecycle, repeated conflicts" },
  "modes": { "headless": "likely one shot with no owner watching", "tab": "likely questions, long runs, or the owner wants to watch" }
}
```

`standard` has no preset: it is the role's active preset (the owner's Control choice). Ship this block in the shipped `imp` role file; adding it to the owner's `~/.hud/roles/imp.json` is the main session's job, not yours. A tier missing from the block is not offered to the Decision API; a role file without the block is never routed. Do not hard-code tier presets or models anywhere in src/.

When on, an `imp` create asks the Decision API for `{tier, mode, reason}`. The input is the brief, ticket text, context-file names and sizes, and the block's `use` texts. Then:
- Run the tier's preset chain. If none of its places is available (harness off, quota exhausted, pre-input launch failure), fall to standard and record `fallback`.
- Headless only when the chosen place's harness supports headless today (pi after 01; claude and agy after 02); otherwise tab, recorded as `mode_reason`.
- Overflow to `general` runs the routed chain (see role-overrides/01 for the unrouted case).
- `retry_of` keeps the tier without a new decision; a land repair of a light job runs as standard.
- Failure, timeout or the toggle off: active preset in a tab, `source: "default"`.

Record `route: {tier, mode, reason, source: "decision"|"default", fallback?}` in job.json. Show it in the create result and `hud_read`. Document the block in docs/reference.md and docs/reference.zh.md.

acceptance.text: With a stub Decision API: a one-file doc brief routes light+headless (tab while agy lacks headless); a cross-module brief routes hard+tab
A role file without `routing`, or missing the `light` tier, never yields that tier
Unavailable tier preset falls to standard with `fallback`; API error or timeout falls back to default+tab and says so
Overflow keeps the routed chain; retry keeps the tier; a light job's land repair runs standard
job.json and hud_read carry the route; targeted tests pass

tickets.title: Milestone review fixes for routing and headless workers
tickets.what:
Fix every blocking finding in `docs/reviews/2026-11-22-auto-route-milestone.md` in one pass (spec 1-5, simplicity 1-3, plus its "What can be deleted" list). The review names files and lines; the design intent it was judged against is in `tmp/tasks/review-auto-route/brief.md`. In short:
- Explicit `mode: "tab"` and `mode: "headless"` both win while routing; routing then asks only for the tier; the continuability check applies only to headless.
- Placement flags (model/thinking) in caller `pi_args` are rejected for roles other than `general`; a `retry_of` that changes role does not carry general's one-job overrides.
- A standard/headless route that cannot launch falls back to the active preset in a tab when mode was not explicit (pre-input only; never replay after input may have reached a worker).
- Inspector output parses Antigravity's `event` records and tells "no output yet" (zero bytes) from "nothing displayable".
- A headless Claude or Antigravity question ends the turn through the runner (keep the native session), not by trusting the model's next reply; `hud_respond` then resumes.
- Unrouted headless jobs fall through to the next compatible place on a pre-input rejection like tab jobs do; the one-shot exception stays for sonic only; direct and queued creates share the rule.
- An expired follow-up to an overflow job keeps imp's launch role and chain.
- Headless pi session identity compares canonical cwd paths.
- Deletions: the blanket headless break, the `retrySource` shadow, the 40-vs-12 output line limit (one shared limit).
Leave the review's optional list alone.

acceptance.text: Each blocking finding has one main-path test that fails before and passes after
Targeted tests pass

tickets.title: A message sent to a working headless job runs as its next turn
tickets.what: Found live 2026-11-22: with routing on, imp jobs start headless, and hud_send (single or {jobs} fan-out) to a working headless job returns not_continuable (sendJob: no primary pane), so the main session cannot steer most working imps. A tab worker queues the message for after its current step; a headless worker should do the same: record the message in the job dir and, when the current turn ends, resume the native session with it as the next turn (same resume path as a post-report send within resume_s). One process per turn stays.

acceptance.text: hud_send and hud_send({jobs}) to a working headless pi, claude or agy job return ok with queued, not not_continuable
When the current turn ends (report or plain turn end), the session resumes with the queued message(s) in send order; nothing is dropped if the turn ends asking (delivered with the hud_respond resume)
The caller's MCP task stays current and wakes at the final report, as for a tab job's queued send (FANOUT-TASK)
Synthetic fake-bin tests for pi and one CLI harness; docs/reference.md (+ zh) headless paragraph says follow-ups to a working headless job run after its current turn

tickets.title: A headless worker's question does not kill its running sonic children
tickets.what: Found live 2026-11-22: land-log/01's headless imp (jfac82c255bad0b73) started sonic j9f55feffc7f77ed5, then called hud_ask; its turn ended at 19:31:12 and the sonic runner died in the same second with no exit receipt (state failed, 'sonic runner exited without an exit receipt', no stderr). Two sonics of a headless imp that never asked survived. So ending a headless turn (ask, or plain turn end) reaps the worker's process tree including detached sonic children. A sonic child is its own job: it must keep running across the parent's turn end, and its result must reach the parent on its next turn (hud_sonic wait / the ready message, as for a pi tab worker; IMP-LEAN-03).

acceptance.text: Synthetic test: a headless pi worker starts a sonic child, then asks; the child keeps running and settles with its report
On the parent's resume (hud_respond), hud_sonic wait returns the child's report; a child that settled while the parent was idle is delivered as a ready message on the next turn
Stop (hud_close / panel stop) of the parent still kills the children; a parent that reports and closes leaves no orphan runner
The same holds for a headless CLI (claude or agy) worker if they can start sonic children
